sentence: A leak damaged six flats in a block of thirty. The residents of those six flats will receive hotel vouchers.
setupText: Choose the wording that uses a defining relative to select the affected residents, not to add information about an already selected group.
taskText: A leak damaged six flats in a block of thirty. The residents of those six flats will receive hotel vouchers.
text: Choose the wording that uses a defining relative to select the affected residents, not to add information about an already selected group. A leak damaged six flats in a block of thirty. The residents of those six flats will receive hotel vouchers.
options: The residents whose flats were damaged will receive hotel vouchers.
The residents, whose flats were damaged, will receive hotel vouchers.
The residents whose flats were unaffected will receive hotel vouchers.
The residents whose hotel stays are ending will receive new vouchers.
answer: The residents whose flats were damaged will receive hotel vouchers.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3181:Restrictive possessive relative selects a subset
explanation: Without commas, whose flats were damaged selects the residents by damage to their flats.

rationales.The residents, whose flats were damaged,: The commas make the damage supplementary information about an already identified group, not the requested defining restriction.
rationales.The residents whose flats were damaged w: Without commas, whose flats were damaged selects the residents by damage to their flats.
rationales.The residents whose flats were unaffecte: Unaffected selects residents outside the damaged flats, reversing eligibility.
rationales.The residents whose hotel stays are endi: This selects residents by the end of a hotel stay, not by damage to their flats.

sentence: The museum extended its evening opening hours, which made it easier for shift workers to visit.
setupText: Choose what 'which' refers to in this sentence.
taskText: The museum extended its evening opening hours, which made it easier for shift workers to visit.
text: Choose what 'which' refers to in this sentence. The museum extended its evening opening hours, which made it easier for shift workers to visit.
options: The shift workers who visited
The museum's evening visitors
The museum's location
The extension of the opening hours
answer: The extension of the opening hours
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3182:Which refers to a preceding event
explanation: 'Which' comments on the preceding event: extending the hours made visits easier.

rationales.The shift workers who visited: Shift workers receive the benefit; they are not what 'which' refers back to.
rationales.The museum's evening visitors: The sentence describes a change in access, not a previously mentioned group of visitors.
rationales.The extension of the opening hours: 'Which' comments on the preceding event: extending the hours made visits easier.
rationales.The museum's location: No location is supplied as an antecedent; the benefit follows the change in hours.

sentence: The officer I handed the documents to recorded the delivery.
setupText: Choose the version suited to a formal report that keeps 'to' immediately before the relative pronoun.
taskText: The officer I handed the documents to recorded the delivery.
text: Choose the version suited to a formal report that keeps 'to' immediately before the relative pronoun. The officer I handed the documents to recorded the delivery.
options: The officer to who I handed the documents recorded the delivery.
The officer to that I handed the documents recorded the delivery.
The officer to whom I handed the documents recorded the delivery.
The officer to whose I handed the documents recorded the delivery.
answer: The officer to whom I handed the documents recorded the delivery.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3183:Formal human relative after a fronted preposition
explanation: 'Whom' is the formal object form after the fronted preposition 'to'; the recipient remains the officer.

rationales.The officer to who I handed the document: In this formal fronted-preposition construction, the report requires 'to whom'; 'who' is natural with a final 'to'.
rationales.The officer to that I handed the documen: 'That' cannot directly follow a fronted preposition in a relative clause.
rationales.The officer to whose I handed the docume: 'Whose' needs a possessed noun, such as 'whose assistant', and cannot stand alone after 'to' here.
rationales.The officer to whom I handed the documen: 'Whom' is the formal object form after the fronted preposition 'to'; the recipient remains the officer.

sentence: The teams negotiated about a plan. Complete: The plan ___ has now been published.
setupText: Choose the relative phrase that preserves the plan as the subject of negotiations, not as a method or source of opposition.
taskText: The teams negotiated about a plan. Complete: The plan ___ has now been published.
text: Choose the relative phrase that preserves the plan as the subject of negotiations, not as a method or source of opposition. The teams negotiated about a plan. Complete: The plan ___ has now been published.
options: through which the teams exchanged proposals
to which the teams attached their agreement
about which the teams negotiated
under which the teams held negotiations
answer: about which the teams negotiated
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3184:A fronted preposition identifies the relative's semantic role
explanation: About which identifies the plan as the topic of the negotiations, preserving the original relationship.

rationales.about which the teams negotiated: About which identifies the plan as the topic of the negotiations, preserving the original relationship.
rationales.through which the teams exchanged propos: Through which presents the plan as a means of exchanging proposals, not their subject.
rationales.to which the teams attached their agreem: To which describes attaching agreement to the plan, not negotiations about it.
rationales.under which the teams held negotiations: Under which makes the plan a framework governing negotiations rather than their topic.

sentence: The application was rejected because it arrived late. The decision letter did not explain that reason.
setupText: Choose the wording that clearly identifies the reason for the rejection.
taskText: The application was rejected because it arrived late. The decision letter did not explain that reason.
text: Choose the wording that clearly identifies the reason for the rejection. The application was rejected because it arrived late. The decision letter did not explain that reason.
options: The application which the letter rejected arrived late.
The letter explaining the rejection arrived late.
The reason why the letter arrived late was the application's rejection.
The reason for which the application was rejected was not explained in the letter.
answer: The reason for which the application was rejected was not explained in the letter.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3185:Formal reason relative with for which
explanation: For which links the reason to the rejection; the main clause preserves its absence from the letter.

rationales.The application which the letter rejecte: This describes the application but does not preserve the failure to explain the reason.
rationales.The letter explaining the rejection arri: This transfers lateness to the letter and says it explained the rejection, contrary to the original.
rationales.The reason for which the application was: For which links the reason to the rejection; the main clause preserves its absence from the letter.
rationales.The reason why the letter arrived late w: This makes rejection the cause of a late letter, reversing and changing the causal facts.

sentence: The town has one dental clinic. It offers free check-ups and will move in June.
setupText: Choose the sentence that presents the clinic's free service as extra information about the already identified clinic.
taskText: The town has one dental clinic. It offers free check-ups and will move in June.
text: Choose the sentence that presents the clinic's free service as extra information about the already identified clinic. The town has one dental clinic. It offers free check-ups and will move in June.
options: The clinic that offers free check-ups will move in June.
The free check-ups which the clinic offers will move in June.
The clinic will offer free check-ups when it moves in June.
The clinic, which offers free check-ups, will move in June.
answer: The clinic, which offers free check-ups, will move in June.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3186:Supplementary relative for an already identified institution
explanation: The comma-separated which clause adds information about the already identified clinic; the move remains the main statement.

rationales.The clinic that offers free check-ups wi: The defining clause uses the service to identify which clinic, instead of presenting it as supplementary information.
rationales.The clinic, which offers free check-ups,: The comma-separated which clause adds information about the already identified clinic; the move remains the main statement.
rationales.The free check-ups which the clinic offe: This makes the check-ups, rather than the clinic, the thing that will move.
rationales.The clinic will offer free check-ups whe: This ties the service to the future move instead of reporting its current availability.

sentence: The survey received eighty responses, half of which came from tenants.
setupText: Choose the interpretation supported by the sentence.
taskText: The survey received eighty responses, half of which came from tenants.
text: Choose the interpretation supported by the sentence. The survey received eighty responses, half of which came from tenants.
options: Half the tenants who were contacted responded.
Forty responses came from tenants.
Eighty tenants supplied half the responses.
Forty tenants were invited to complete the survey.
answer: Forty responses came from tenants.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3187:Partitive relative quantifies the antecedent set
explanation: Which refers to the eighty responses; half of that set is forty.

rationales.Half the tenants who were contacted resp: Half of which quantifies responses, not the proportion of contacted tenants who replied.
rationales.Eighty tenants supplied half the respons: Eighty is the total response count, not the number of tenant respondents.
rationales.Forty tenants were invited to complete t: The relative counts responses received, not people invited to participate.
Which refers to the eighty responses; half of that set is forty.

sentence: We borrowed tools from a neighbour. The tools were stored in her garage.
setupText: Choose the version that keeps both the owner and the place of storage unchanged.
taskText: We borrowed tools from a neighbour. The tools were stored in her garage.
text: Choose the version that keeps both the owner and the place of storage unchanged. We borrowed tools from a neighbour. The tools were stored in her garage.
options: The neighbour whose tools we stored in our garage borrowed them from us.
The neighbour in whose garage the tools were stored lent them to us.
The neighbour whose garage we borrowed stored our tools there.
The neighbour from whose garage we removed our tools borrowed them.
answer: The neighbour in whose garage the tools were stored lent them to us.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3188:Preposition plus whose and a possessed noun
explanation: In whose garage preserves storage in the neighbour's garage, and lent them to us preserves the loan direction.

rationales.The neighbour in whose garage the tools: In whose garage preserves storage in the neighbour's garage, and lent them to us preserves the loan direction.
rationales.The neighbour whose tools we stored in o: This changes her garage to ours and makes us the lenders.
rationales.The neighbour whose garage we borrowed s: This makes the garage the borrowed object and the tools ours.
rationales.The neighbour from whose garage we remov: This makes the tools ours and the neighbour their borrower, reversing the original loan.

sentence: The software stores invoices. Our accountant recommended it.
setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves the two separate descriptions of the software.
taskText: The software stores invoices. Our accountant recommended it.
text: Choose the sentence that preserves the two separate descriptions of the software. The software stores invoices. Our accountant recommended it.
options: The accountant who stores invoices recommended the software.
The software that stores invoices is the one our accountant recommended.
The software our accountant designed stores invoices.
The software that creates invoices is the one our accountant recommended.
answer: The software that stores invoices is the one our accountant recommended.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3189:Subject and object relatives referring to the same thing
explanation: That stores invoices is a subject relative; our accountant recommended is an object relative identifying the same software.

rationales.The accountant who stores invoices recom: This makes the accountant the person storing invoices, rather than describing a software function.
rationales.The software our accountant designed sto: Designed replaces a recommendation with authorship of the software.
rationales.The software that stores invoices is the: That stores invoices is a subject relative; our accountant recommended is an object relative identifying the same software.
rationales.The software that creates invoices is th: Creating invoices is a different function from storing them.

sentence: We postponed the launch, a decision which the designers welcomed.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that keeps the relative clause attached to the decision.
taskText: We postponed the launch, a decision which the designers welcomed.
text: Choose the interpretation that keeps the relative clause attached to the decision. We postponed the launch, a decision which the designers welcomed.
options: The designers welcomed the product that was due to launch.
The designers proposed the postponement themselves.
The designers approved of postponing the launch.
The designers approved of the original launch date.
answer: The designers approved of postponing the launch.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3190:An explicit summary noun anchors relative reference
explanation: A decision explicitly identifies the postponement as what the designers welcomed.

rationales.The designers welcomed the product that: Which describes a decision, not the product itself.
rationales.The designers approved of postponing the: A decision explicitly identifies the postponement as what the designers welcomed.
rationales.The designers proposed the postponement: Welcoming a decision does not establish who proposed it.
rationales.The designers approved of the original l: Welcoming the postponement does not mean approving the original launch date.

sentence: There are exactly two versions of the brochure. Each contains an outdated phone number.
setupText: Choose the wording that clearly says both documents contain the error.
taskText: There are exactly two versions of the brochure. Each contains an outdated phone number.
text: Choose the wording that clearly says both documents contain the error. There are exactly two versions of the brochure. Each contains an outdated phone number.
options: The brochures, both of which contain an outdated number, are being reprinted.
The brochures which contain an outdated number are being reprinted.
The brochures, one of which contains an outdated number, are being reprinted.
The brochure whose number is outdated is being reprinted.
answer: The brochures, both of which contain an outdated number, are being reprinted.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3191:Explicit exhaustive reference with both of which
explanation: Both of which explicitly applies the outdated-number description to the two brochures.

rationales.The brochures which contain an outdated: This selects brochures by the error but does not explicitly say both versions have it.
rationales.The brochures, one of which contains an: One of which specifies one version, not the required fact about each of the two.
rationales.The brochures, both of which contain an: Both of which explicitly applies the outdated-number description to the two brochures.
rationales.The brochure whose number is outdated is: The singular brochure identifies one version and leaves the other unaccounted for.

sentence: We paid what the supplier had charged, then requested an itemized receipt.
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'what' in this sentence.
taskText: We paid what the supplier had charged, then requested an itemized receipt.
text: Choose the meaning of 'what' in this sentence. We paid what the supplier had charged, then requested an itemized receipt.
options: The reason the supplier had charged it
The time when the supplier had sent the charge
The person whom the supplier had charged
The amount the supplier had charged
answer: The amount the supplier had charged
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3192:What combines a head and a relative relationship
explanation: 'What' combines an amount with a relative link: the amount that the supplier had charged was paid.

rationales.The amount the supplier had charged: 'What' combines an amount with a relative link: the amount that the supplier had charged was paid.
rationales.The reason the supplier had charged it: A reason is not the object of 'paid' here; 'what' identifies the amount paid.
rationales.The time when the supplier had sent the: The phrase supplies what was paid, not when a charge was sent.
rationales.The person whom the supplier had charged: The supplier is the payment recipient; 'what' identifies the charged amount, not a billed person.

sentence: I learned about the vacancy from a former colleague. The former colleague now works abroad. Complete: The former colleague ___ now works abroad.
setupText: Choose the phrase that preserves the stated source of the information.
taskText: I learned about the vacancy from a former colleague. The former colleague now works abroad. Complete: The former colleague ___ now works abroad.
text: Choose the phrase that preserves the stated source of the information. I learned about the vacancy from a former colleague. The former colleague now works abroad. Complete: The former colleague ___ now works abroad.
options: from whom I learned about the vacancy
to whom I explained the vacancy
with whom I applied for the vacancy
for whom I found out about the vacancy
answer: from whom I learned about the vacancy
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3193:Prepositions distinguish source, recipient, companion, and beneficiary
explanation: From whom preserves the colleague as the source from which the speaker learned about the job.

rationales.to whom I explained the vacancy: To whom makes the colleague a recipient of the speaker's explanation, not the source of information.
rationales.from whom I learned about the vacancy: From whom preserves the colleague as the source from which the speaker learned about the job.
rationales.with whom I applied for the vacancy: With whom makes the colleague a fellow applicant, which the original does not say.
rationales.for whom I found out about the vacancy: For whom makes the colleague the beneficiary of an inquiry, not necessarily its information source.

sentence: Staff announced a change during a meeting. That meeting lasted an hour.
setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves the meeting as the occasion of the announcement.
taskText: Staff announced a change during a meeting. That meeting lasted an hour.
text: Choose the sentence that preserves the meeting as the occasion of the announcement. Staff announced a change during a meeting. That meeting lasted an hour.
options: The meeting at which the staff announced the change lasted an hour.
The meeting for which staff prepared an announcement lasted an hour.
The meeting that the staff announced lasted an hour.
The meeting which the staff changed lasted an hour.
answer: The meeting at which the staff announced the change lasted an hour.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3194:Event antecedent as occasion rather than object
explanation: At which makes the meeting the occasion, with staff as announcers and the change as their announced subject.

rationales.The meeting for which staff prepared an: Preparing an announcement for a meeting does not say it was actually made during that meeting.
rationales.The meeting that the staff announced las: This makes the meeting itself the thing announced, not the occasion of a separate announcement.
rationales.The meeting which the staff changed last: This says the staff altered the meeting rather than announced a change there.
rationales.The meeting at which the staff announced: At which makes the meeting the occasion, with staff as announcers and the change as their announced subject.

sentence: I spoke to the technician who the receptionist said would repair the scanner.
setupText: Choose the conclusion supported by the sentence.
taskText: I spoke to the technician who the receptionist said would repair the scanner.
text: Choose the conclusion supported by the sentence. I spoke to the technician who the receptionist said would repair the scanner.
options: The receptionist will repair the scanner.
The technician said the receptionist would repair it.
The speaker told the technician to replace the scanner.
The receptionist identified the technician as the expected repairer.
answer: The receptionist identified the technician as the expected repairer.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3195:Relative subject across an embedded reporting clause
explanation: The relative refers to the technician across the embedded phrase the receptionist said.

rationales.The receptionist will repair the scanner: The receptionist is the subject of said; the technician is the understood subject of would repair.
rationales.The technician said the receptionist wou: This swaps the speaker of the report and the expected repairer.
rationales.The receptionist identified the technici: The relative refers to the technician across the embedded phrase the receptionist said.
rationales.The speaker told the technician to repla: The main clause reports a conversation, not an instruction to replace the equipment.

sentence: A warehouse stands beside our office. Its roof was damaged in the storm.
setupText: Choose the sentence that reports damage to the roof, not to the neighbouring property.
taskText: A warehouse stands beside our office. Its roof was damaged in the storm.
text: Choose the sentence that reports damage to the roof, not to the neighbouring property. A warehouse stands beside our office. Its roof was damaged in the storm.
options: The office beside which the warehouse stands had a damaged roof.
The warehouse whose roof was damaged stands beside our office.
The warehouse beside our damaged office has a new roof.
The office whose roof was damaged stands beside the warehouse.
answer: The warehouse whose roof was damaged stands beside our office.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3196:Inanimate whose and nearby competing antecedents
explanation: Whose ties the damaged roof to the warehouse, and the main clause preserves its position beside the office.

rationales.The warehouse whose roof was damaged sta: Whose ties the damaged roof to the warehouse, and the main clause preserves its position beside the office.
rationales.The office beside which the warehouse st: This assigns the damaged roof to the office rather than the warehouse.
rationales.The warehouse beside our damaged office: This describes the office as damaged and introduces an unstated new roof.
rationales.The office whose roof was damaged stands: The relative again makes the office the owner of the damaged roof.

sentence: The guest speaker finished her presentation, at which point the audience began asking questions.
setupText: Choose the interpretation of 'at which point'.
taskText: The guest speaker finished her presentation, at which point the audience began asking questions.
text: Choose the interpretation of 'at which point'. The guest speaker finished her presentation, at which point the audience began asking questions.
options: Questions continued throughout the presentation.
The speaker finished after answering the questions.
Questions began when the presentation ended.
The audience chose a place to ask questions later.
answer: Questions began when the presentation ended.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3197:At which point relates a new event to the immediately preceding event
explanation: 'Which' refers back to the finishing event, and 'at which point' uses that event as the time for questions to begin.

rationales.Questions continued throughout the prese: 'At which point' locates the start of questions at the presentation's end, not throughout it.
rationales.Questions began when the presentation en: 'Which' refers back to the finishing event, and 'at which point' uses that event as the time for questions to begin.
rationales.The speaker finished after answering the: The presentation finishes before the questions begin, not after they have been answered.
rationales.The audience chose a place to ask questi: 'Point' is a moment in the sequence here, not a physical place chosen for later use.

sentence: The specialist to whom the nurse referred me has moved to another clinic.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that preserves the referral direction.
taskText: The specialist to whom the nurse referred me has moved to another clinic.
text: Choose the interpretation that preserves the referral direction. The specialist to whom the nurse referred me has moved to another clinic.
options: The nurse directed the speaker to the specialist.
The specialist referred the nurse to the speaker.
The speaker referred the nurse to the specialist.
The nurse received a referral from the specialist.
answer: The nurse directed the speaker to the specialist.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3198:Three participant roles in a formal relative
explanation: The nurse made the referral, me received it, and to whom points to the specialist as the destination.

rationales.The specialist referred the nurse to the: The nurse, not the specialist, is the subject of referred in the relative clause.
rationales.The speaker referred the nurse to the sp: Me is the person referred, not the person making the referral.
rationales.The nurse received a referral from the s: To whom identifies the referral's destination; it does not make the specialist its source.
rationales.The nurse directed the speaker to the sp: The nurse made the referral, me received it, and to whom points to the specialist as the destination.

sentence: We may reach a point where further discussion will not help.
setupText: Choose the paraphrase that preserves the abstract meaning of 'point where'.
taskText: We may reach a point where further discussion will not help.
text: Choose the paraphrase that preserves the abstract meaning of 'point where'. We may reach a point where further discussion will not help.
options: We may find a place where discussion will be easier to hear.
We may establish a rule under which discussion is not permitted.
We may reach a stage at which more discussion is no longer useful.
We may choose a subject on which discussion will be helpful.
answer: We may reach a stage at which more discussion is no longer useful.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3199:Abstract where after point
explanation: 'Point where' describes a stage in the process when continuing the discussion stops being useful.

rationales.We may reach a stage at which more discu: 'Point where' describes a stage in the process when continuing the discussion stops being useful.
rationales.We may find a place where discussion wil: This makes 'point' a physical location and changes usefulness to audibility.
rationales.We may establish a rule under which disc: 'Not helping' is an assessment of usefulness, not a prohibition on discussion.
rationales.We may choose a subject on which discuss: The original identifies a stage at which discussion ceases to help, not a useful subject for it.

sentence: The instructions lack the detail that beginners need to complete the installation.
setupText: Choose the paraphrase that preserves what the relative clause says is missing.
taskText: The instructions lack the detail that beginners need to complete the installation.
text: Choose the paraphrase that preserves what the relative clause says is missing. The instructions lack the detail that beginners need to complete the installation.
options: Beginners lack the instructions that experts need.
The instructions omit information necessary for beginners.
The installation needs beginners to supply more detail.
The instructions contain details that beginners can omit.
answer: The instructions omit information necessary for beginners.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b2-3200:An object relative specifies needed but absent information
explanation: That beginners need identifies the absent detail by its role in helping beginners complete the task.

rationales.Beginners lack the instructions that exp: This changes missing content inside the instructions into beginners not possessing instructions.
rationales.The installation needs beginners to supp: Beginners need the detail; the original does not assign them the task of supplying it.
rationales.The instructions omit information necess: That beginners need identifies the absent detail by its role in helping beginners complete the task.
rationales.The instructions contain details that be: Can omit contradicts need and changes absent material into included material.
